:::{#def-kfold}
#### $\nfolds$-fold cross-validation

In **$\nfolds$-fold cross-validation**:

1. The data are randomly divided into $\nfolds$ [folds](#def-folds) of equal, or nearly equal, size.
2. For each fold $\fold{\ifold}$, $\ifold = 1, \ldots, \nfolds$:
   - Fit the model to all data *except* fold $\fold{\ifold}$,
     giving the [fold-out rule](#def-fold-out-rule) $\fittedwo{\ifold}{\cdot}$.
   - Compute predicted values for the observations in fold $\fold{\ifold}$.
3. Compute a summary prediction-error measure across all folds.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#rem-kfold-vs-validation-set}
#### Cross-validation instead of a single validation set

If data are limited,
$\nfolds$-fold cross-validation
can replace the single validation set of @def-data-splits
for more stable tuning.
In @exr-kfold, $\nfolds = 4$ folds of 8 cars each
give 4 fits on 24 cars each.
:::
